stgs.name: Aggression
targets: Decrease instances of Physical Aggression
Decrease instances of Verbal Aggression

stgs.name: Compliance
targets: Reduce instances of non-compliance
Decrease instances of prompt dependency
Decrease instances of Disruptive Joking
Reduce instances of task refusal

stgs.name: Impolite Behavior
targets: Decrease instances of impolite interrupting
Decrease instances of complaining
Decrease the use of inappropriate language

stgs.name: Elopement
targets: Decrease instances of Elopement

stgs.name: Silly Behaviors
targets: Decrease instances of silly behaviors

stgs.name: Tantrums
targets: Decrease tantrum behaviors
Reduce the duration of tantrum behaviors

stgs.name: Off Task Behaviors
targets: Decrease instances of engaging in unexpected behaviors
Decrease instances of inappropriate/annoying touch to peers

stgs.name: Property Destruction
targets: Decrease instances of property destruction

stgs.name: Unsafe Behaviors
targets: Decrease unsafe behaviors

stgs.name: Compliance
targets: Comply with therapist instructions during session
Follow instructions given by the group leader in the absence of maladaptive behaviors
Maintain appropriate body orientation during sessions (feet on the ground, hands on the table, and head and body facing the technician)
Comply with the therapist's request to begin undesired task
Comply with tedious tasks such as reading and writing and begin with no prompting necessary
Comply to all adult directives aside from therapist

stgs.name: Attention
targets: Maintain focused attention on a non-preferred or play task for 5 minutes
Sustain focus on a task for 5 minutes while ignoring minor distractions e.g., peer noise, movement in the room
Divide attention between two tasks e.g., listening to instructions while completing written work for 3 minutes

stgs.name: Task Persistence
targets: Persist in completing a non-preferred or moderately challenging task for up to 5 minutes

stgs.name: Delayed Gratification
targets: Delay gratification by waiting up to 2 minutes for a preferred item or activity when told "wait,"

stgs.name: Effort Over Time
targets: Sustain effort on a multi-step functional task until completion,

stgs.name: Staying Within Boundaries
targets: Ask permission respectfully before leaving a session or room

stgs.name: Resilience
targets: Respond to a failure or setback e.g., making an error, losing a game by using a positive coping response e.g., saying "I'll try again," taking a deep breath

stgs.name: Flexibility
targets: Display flexibility by tolerating situations where things don't go as expected or desired
Demonstrate tolerance of frustration by responding calmly to a setback through the use of an appropriate coping strategy

stgs.name: Tantrum Replacement Behaviors
targets: Respond appropriately and respectfully

stgs.name: Group Instruction
targets: Respond appropriately to a group directive by initiating the expected action within 10 seconds
Respond appropriately to a group directive given during group instruction within 10 seconds

stgs.name: Functional Instructions
targets: Follow a functional instruction in a daily context within 15 seconds

stgs.name: Temporal Directions
targets: Follow a sequenced instruction of 2-3 steps in order

stgs.name: Categorization
targets: Categorize 2 objects and situations

stgs.name: Compare and Contrast
targets: Compare and contrast by finding similarities and differences between 2 objects and 2 situations

stgs.name: Self Advocacy
targets: Appropriately communicate personal needs when prompted in various settings

Clearly and audibly say the word "no" when prompted with a choice or activity they do not wish to partake in. The response should be within 5 seconds of the prompt and must be made in an appropriate tone and volume.
Ask for help with a difficult task
Ask for help if he feels overwhelmed by a transition
Verbally describe progress on his own task performance

stgs.name: Manding
targets: Identify Personal Need for a Break and Communicate It
Appropriately ask for a break when he needs one, such as saying "I need a break",
Ask to shorten skill coaching discussions to a reasonable time, such as 3 minutes,
Mand for attention appropriately from the technician
Mand for attention appropriately from peers

stgs.name: Asking for Help
targets: Ask for help with a difficult task

stgs.name: Conversation Skills
targets: Engage in a back-and-forth conversation with 4 exchanges
Speak in full sentences during conversations, avoiding 1-2 word answers
Stay on topic for at least 3 conversational turns
Ask for time after or during a conversation to tell jokes such as during a lull in the conversation or after important points have been made and the discussion is at a less serious turn
Demonstrate Basic Respectful Behavior, Like Listening When Others Speak, in 1 Activity
Engage in Simple Conversational Exchanges with the Therapist, Like Answering Questions
Maintain a conversation for 4 conversational turns
Stay on the topic of the conversation for at least 3 conversational turns
Increase the duration in which he engages in conversational exchanges for up to 1 minute, in the absence of maladaptive behaviors
Identify 3 contrived communication breakdowns and 1 possible solution to each

stgs.name: Asking Questions
targets: Initiate questions during verbal interactions in various settings

stgs.name: Answering Questions
targets: Use full sentences of at least 5-7 words to respond to questions or contribute to a conversation

stgs.name: Initiating Conversations
targets: Initiate an appropriate conversation with a peer
Wait 2 minutes before trying to politely interrupt
Greet the other person when appropriate

stgs.name: Wait Time and Turn-Taking
targets: Wait 10 seconds before saying 'I don't know' in response to a question posed to him
Wait until the adult pauses before he says what he wants to
Wait until the peer pauses before he says what he wants to say
Use a verbal cue such as "excuse me" before interjecting when others are speaking

stgs.name: Using Proper Tone and Volume
targets: Use the proper tone and volume for different situations
Use a calm tone of voice to discuss when he thinks he was treated unfairly

stgs.name: Manners and Politeness
targets: Use Polite Phrases or Gestures, Like Saying "Thank You" or "Excuse Me," in Appropriate Situations
Accept a Differing Opinion from an Adult in a Constructive Manner Without Arguing
Accept a Differing Opinion from a Peer in a Constructive Manner Without Arguing
Express a Differing Opinion in a Constructive Manner Without Arguing
Show Respectful Behavior for 3 rounds of conversation, Like Listening or Nodding, When Interacting with an Adult

stgs.name: Responding Appropriately
targets: Respond within 3 seconds when spoken to during verbal interactions in various settings
Accept a 30-second latency from when he requests an item until he receives the item without engaging in maladaptive behaviors
Acknowledge a Peer's Comment or Action with a Nod or Brief Verbal Response
Acknowledge and Correct a False Statement
Respond to Requests from Adults with a Calm 'Yes' or an Appropriate Alternative Suggestion

stgs.name: Accepting Feedback
targets: Respond to Feedback with a Simple Acknowledgment or Thank You

stgs.name: Role-Playing Social Skills
targets: Use Role-Playing to Practice Appropriate Social Responses and Behaviors in 1 Scenario

stgs.name: Honesty
targets: Discuss the Consequences of Dishonesty and Identify Alternatives in 1 Scenario

stgs.name: Conflict Resolution
targets: Use Basic Conflict Resolution Strategies, Like Asking for Help from an Adult, in a Disagreement with Peers

stgs.name: Following Directions
targets: Follow 2 step directives that involve distance

stgs.name: Retelling Information
targets: Independently retell one activity or discussion that occurred during the therapy session
Use necessary details when retelling an activity or discussion from the therapy session
Retell a daily experience including 2 expanded details and one personal connection,

stgs.name: Inferencing
targets: Answer 1 inferencing question after hearing or reading a short story
Identify the logical next step in a short written or spoken scenario
Predict the expected answer or outcome in a short written prompt

stgs.name: Tacting Emotions
targets: Identify their emotions without using profane language when they are frustrated, angry, sad etc.

stgs.name: Emotion Recognition
targets: Identify Basic Emotions in Himself or Others, Such as Happiness or Frustration, in Contrived Scenarios
Identify and verbalize the feelings of others when presented with a contrived or hypothetical scenario
Identify and verbalize the feelings of others in natural, real-world scenarios

stgs.name: Understanding Others
targets: Identify and verbalize the perspective of another person when presented with a contrived or hypothetical scenario
Identify and verbalize the perspective of another person in natural, real world scenarios
Accept another person's opinion or view
Compromise or apologize for what he did when given another's perspective with prompt
Describe one alternative point of view of a contrived social situation
Figure out someone else's perspective in a contrived scenario
Identify possible reasons for another's actions
Demonstrate social awareness by observing peer reactions to a situation and adjusting their own response accordingly

stgs.name: Size of Problem
targets: Label a minor everyday problem and state or demonstrate an independent problem-solving strategy
Label a small problem in a natural setting and use a defined coping or problem-solving strategy
Label a medium-sized problem that requires adult help and use an appropriate help-seeking strategy
Identify a big problem lasting weeks or months, requiring multiple adults and communicate an appropriate coping or help-seeking response
Identify one "big problem" (lasting weeks/months and typically requiring involvement from multiple adults/services) and communicate an appropriate coping or help-seeking response
Identify a huge problem e.g., emergency requiring immediate group response and follow established safety procedures

Demonstrate a constructive response to an error by engaging in observable problem-solving e.g., correcting work, asking for help and using at least one positive statement e.g., "I'll try again" following a mistake

stgs.name: Solutions
targets: Identify 1 solution when presented with a problem in a contrived setting
State one workable solution when presented with a contrived problem scenario
Verbalize their initial reaction to a problem and restate it in a constructive manner

stgs.name: Positive Self-Statements
targets: Independently use a positive self-statement about their appearance e.g., "I look nice today" during a social interaction across school and home settings

stgs.name: Initiating with Others
targets: Initiate a game or activity with a peer by approaching peer and asking "do you want to play?" in various social settings
Identify 2 Ways to Respectfully initiate conversations with peers
Offer a compliment to a peer
Utilize a shared interest to initiate a conversation with a peer

stgs.name: Interacting with Peers
targets: Accept a compliment from a peer/adult graciously such as with a thank you
Acknowledge a Peer's Comment or Action with a Nod or Brief Verbal Response
Identify one interest he shares with a peer
Play fairly and follow the rules in a game
Identify a realistic reaction to a contrived social initiation
Identify and acknowledge a contribution made by a peer to a game or group project

stgs.name: Joining Peers
targets: Identify 1 activity that peers may welcome him to join, like a game or conversation
Suggest or Join a Structured Play Activity with Peers, Like a Sports Game or Art Project, for 2 minutes per opportunity
Respond to compliments with a clear, polite verbal reply e.g., "thank you," "I appreciate that" during social interactions

stgs.name: Sharing Personal Information
targets: Tolerate discussion and reflect on how his own personal likes and dislikes are similar or different from a peer or adult

stgs.name: Group Skills
targets: Actively participate in the group discussion by asking/answering a question posed by the group leader
Engage in an Activity Common among Peers, Like Discussing a Popular Toy or Playing a Trending Game
Initiate a verbal interaction with a peer in the social setting
Join in group discussions
Join group activities during group instruction

stgs.name: Social Cues
targets: Demonstrate recognition of facial and gestural cues made by an adult
Demonstrate recognition of facial and gestural cues made by a peer

stgs.name: Following Environmental Expectations
targets: Follow the expectations of his environment

stgs.name: Personal Space
targets: Demonstrate an understanding and respect of personal space by maintaining appropriate physical distance
Maintain appropriate distance from adult when conversing
Maintain appropriate distance from peer when conversing

stgs.name: Respecting Boundaries and Property
targets: Ask before touching or using another person's belongings during activities

stgs.name: Following Single-Step Directions
targets: Successfully Follow a One-Step Instruction, Such as "Please Hand Me the Book,"

stgs.name: Appropriate Alternatives
targets: State an appropriate alternative action to throwing out useful items (e.g., "put it in my backpack/return it to the bin/label it") for 3 different items

stgs.name: Understanding Authority and Roles
targets: Identify the next two levels of authority above self for a given setting and state "who answers to who and why" (one role - who they report to - one brief reason)
Follow the appropriate chain of command using a 3-step script: gain attention - state issue - request help/permission, and explain why that person is in charge.
Respond to questions demonstrating awareness of his role in the environment
Respond to questions demonstrating awareness of others' roles in the environment

stgs.name: Leisure Skills
targets: Choose and Engage in a Simple Activity, Like Reading or Drawing, during unstructured time

stgs.name: Personal Hygiene
targets: Make sure his face is clean after finishing a meal or snack

stgs.name: Organizational Skills
targets: Organize His personal belongings
Organize personal belongings by placing items in labeled areas at session end
Check for and secure personal belongings before leaving an area during transitions

stgs.name: Understanding Item Function
targets: Identify the primary function of common items

stgs.name: Cause and Effect
targets: Explain the cause-and-effect of discarding a useful item by naming one realistic consequence (e.g., "then I can't use it") for 3 different items

stgs.name: Transitions
targets: Use a verbal or visual signal to ask for an additional 2 minutes to finish his current activity
Prepare for and Move from one Activity to another, within 2 Minutes of a Verbal Prompt

stgs.name: Completing Non-Preferred Tasks
targets: Initiate a non preferred task without getting distracted by other activity or task, upon deciding to do an activity or being given instructions to work on a given task
Clean up around his spot after eating

stgs.name: Staying on Task
targets: Stay focused on task/activity until the task/activity is complete

stgs.name: Self Image and Achievement
targets: Share 1 Personal Achievement,
Set a Personal Goal and Take 1 Step Towards Achieving It

stgs.name: Self Monitoring
targets: Utilize a self-monitoring tool to manage his age-appropriate behaviors

stgs.name: Responsibility for Actions
targets: Acknowledge Responsibility for a Personal Action

stgs.name: Flexibility and Tolerance
targets: Tolerate another peer when he feels the game is not fair with prompt
Tolerate discussion and identify his personal likes and dislikes

stgs.name: Coping Skills
targets: Practice Coping Strategies for Challenging Situations
Select and perform an appropriate coping strategy in response to a contrived challenging-situation cue during Discrete Trial Training (DTT), with ≤2 verbal prompts.
Utilize a confusion scale to identify how confused they are with the task in demand
Utilize coping strategies such as using deep breathing or a stress ball during stressful conversations
Identify a situation that will trigger intense emotions
Answer three questions to help him label the size of a problem accurately
Respond to a no-problem situation e.g., minor inconvenience, waiting, or change in plans by demonstrating calm and socially acceptable behavior

stgs.name: Waiting and Impulse Control
targets: Hold back for minimum of 5 minutes when told not to do something
Wait until the timer rings without continuously asking to gain access to reinforcing activity

stgs.name: Following the BIP
targets: Caregiver will implement the Behavior Intervention Plan as written during target routines Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregiver will deliver programmed reinforcement according to the specified schedule 3 times per session with 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregiver will apply the planned consequence procedure when a defined maladaptive behavior occurs Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.

stgs.name: Recording & Tracking
targets: Caregiver will record frequency and intensity rating for the target behavior in identified home routines Once Per Session with a Visual Cue and 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregiver will complete ABC entries for recorded incidents 3 times per session with 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregiver will provide a brief progress/generalization rating with an example Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.

stgs.name: Delivering Reinforcement
targets: Caregiver will deliver positive reinforcement contingent on the identified replacement behavior 3 times per session with 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregiver will acknowledge, prompt as needed, and reinforce functional communication (FCT) Once Per Session with 2 Verbal Prompts.
Caregiver will operate the token economy with correct criteria and exchange for 10 minutes Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.

stgs.name: Supporting Generalization
targets: Caregiver will set up a play or activity to practice a targeted social skill and provide feedback Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregiver will follow the task analysis and prompting plan for an ADL routine Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregiver will prompt and reinforce the target communication skill across two natural routines 3 times per session with 1 Verbal Prompt.

stgs.name: Proactive & Reactive Strategies
targets: Caregiver will implement two antecedent strategies (e.g., visual schedule, choices) before target routines Once Per Session with a Visual Cue.
Caregiver will follow the response flow during incidents (safety - neutral response - teach/reinforce replacement) Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregivers in the home will apply the agreed discipline strategies as written Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.

stgs.name: Prompting & Modeling
targets: Caregiver will create motivating situations and use least-to-most prompts for the target mand 3 times per session with 2 Verbal Prompts.
Caregiver will apply the specified prompting hierarchy with a 3-5s wait time in a skill routine Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregiver will model the target language and social behavior during a daily activity Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.

stgs.name: Supporting Regulation
targets: Caregiver will cue and reinforce a taught coping strategy (e.g., deep breaths, break card) at early signs of escalation Once Per Session with 2 Verbal Prompts.
Caregiver will run the regulation routine (identify feeling, choose tool, reflect) for 2 minutes Per Session with a Visual Cue and 1 Verbal Prompt.
Caregiver will use a calm voice, brief statements, and planned positioning during escalations Once Per Session with 1 Verbal Prompt.

stgs.name: Training & Follow-Through
targets: Caregiver will attend scheduled parent training and participate Once Per Session independently.
Caregiver will provide a concise home progress summary with one example Once Per Session with a Reminder.
Caregiver will implement the assigned home practice plan and submit a permanent product (photo/video/data) Once Per Session with a Reminder.
